subtitle: When Three Crowns Clashed on the Salt Wind Plains

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of battlefield with three different royal banners facing each other under a stormy sky
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan II stands in war chariot at the head of Pandya lines, spear raised, facing distant Chera and Chola hosts massed across the dusty plain of Talaiyalanganam, the sea haze and dark clouds framing the clash to come.

dialogue.text: In the dim Sangam age, when three crowned kings fought for Tamilakam, a young Pandya rode to Talaiyalanganam, broke an alliance of rivals, and carried home a captive king.

i18n.hi: धुंधली संगम उम्र में, जब तीन मुकुट वाले राजा तमिळकम के लिए लड़ रहे थे, एक युवा पांड्य तलैयालंगानम दौड़ा, दुश्मनों की साँठगाँठ तोड़ी, और एक बंदी राजा को घर ले आया।

panels.shot: wide aerial over old Madurai with its fort walls, palace and temple-tanks at dawn
panels.action: The early morning light washes over ancient Madurai’s encircling walls, crowded streets, temple-tanks and palace complex, smoke from hearths rising as the Vaigai river glints beyond.

dialogue.text: The bards call it Madurai of the fragrant groves, jewel of the Pandyas, where kings were weighed against justice and poets against truth.

i18n.hi: भाट इसे सुगंधित उपवनों की मदुरै कहते हैं, पांड्यों का रत्न, जहाँ राजाओं को न्याय से और कवियों को सच्चाई से तौला जाता था।

panels.shot: medium interior shot inside Madurai palace hall, on a young king seated on the throne listening to poets
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan II sits upright on a carved throne in a pillared hall, youthful but composed, as bearded Sangam poets recite, courtiers and generals watching silently.

dialogue.text: Here sat Nedunjeliyan, young Pandya of the broad spear. The poems praise his justice, his gifts, and above all, his hunger to match the war-glory of his ancestors.

i18n.hi: यहीं बैठता था नेडुंजेलियन, चौड़े भाले वाला युवा पांड्य। कविताएँ उसके न्याय, उसकी दानशीलता, और सबसे ज़्यादा उसके उस जोश की तारीफ़ करती हैं जो पूर्वजों की युद्ध-कीर्ति से टक्कर लेना चाहता था।

panels.shot: close-up on Nedunjeliyan’s face in half-shadow as a messenger whispers in his ear
panels.action: In the half-lit audience hall, a dusty messenger leans to murmur urgent news into Nedunjeliyan’s ear; the king’s eyes narrow, jaw tightening as he listens.

dialogue.text: But outside Madurai’s groves, three crowns scraped against each other. Chera and Chola, long rivals, now watched the Pandya throne with wary eyes.

i18n.hi: पर मदुरै के उपवनों के बाहर, तीनों मुकुट एक-दूसरे से रगड़ खा रहे थे। चेरा और चोल, पुराने दुश्मन, अब पांड्य सिंहासन को शक भरी नज़र से देख रहे थे।

panels.shot: map-like overhead stylized shot of the Tamil south with three emblems marking Pandya, Chera and Chola domains
panels.action: A stylized parchment map of the Tamil south shows mountain-fringed Chera lands to the west, Kaveri-fed Chola plains to the east, and Pandya country in the south, each marked with its distinct royal emblem.

dialogue.text: The bards sing of the three crowned kings, mūvēndhar: Chera of the western hills and ports, Chola of the Kaveri, Pandya of Madurai and the southern coasts.

i18n.hi: भाट तीन मुकुटधारी राजाओं, मूवेंधर, का गान करते हैं: पश्चिमी पहाड़ों और बंदरों का चेरा, कावेरी वाला चोल, मदुरै और दक्षिणी तटों का पांड्य।

panels.shot: medium shot in war council, top view of a low table with counters as generals gesture
panels.action: In a lamplit chamber, Nedunjeliyan leans over a low map-table strewn with stones and tiny banners, while veteran commanders point to the coast near Talaiyalanganam, faces tense in debate.

dialogue.text: Some tradition hints that Chera and Chola forces drew together near the eastern coast. The poems do not list their councils, but they remember the answer from Madurai.

i18n.hi: कुछ परंपराएँ इशारा करती हैं कि चेरा–चोल सेनाएँ पूरबी तट के पास साथ आ खड़ी हुईं। कविताएँ उनकी परिषदें नहीं गिनतीं, बस मदुरै से आया जवाब याद रखती हैं।

panels.shot: medium low-angle on Nedunjeliyan rising from council, hand on sword-hilt
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan rises from his seat in the war council, hand resting on his sword-hilt, his expression resolute as elders around him bow slightly.

dialogue.speaker: nedunjeliyan_ii
dialogue.text: If they gather in another’s land, let them scatter at my spear.

i18n.hi: अगर वे दूसरे की धरती पर जुटें, तो मेरे भाले से बिखरेंगे।

panels.shot: wide dynamic shot of Pandya army marching out of Madurai gate
panels.action: Columns of Pandya infantry, elephant corps, and chariots roll out through Madurai’s great gate in a cloud of dust; Nedunjeliyan’s chariot leads, banners streaming in the hot wind.

dialogue.text: The Maduraikanci praises him as one who did not wait behind walls. He carried war into rival country, choosing the salt-wind plains of Talaiyalanganam as his answer.

i18n.hi: मदुरैकांजी उसे दीवारों के पीछे न ठहरने वाला कहकर सराहती है। वह खुद लड़ाई को दुश्मन की धरती पर ले गया, और तलैयालंगानम के नमकीन मैदानों को अपना जवाब चुना।

panels.shot: long wide shot of the coastal plain of Talaiyalanganam with distant sea and two armies facing
panels.action: On a broad coastal plain backed by a hazy strip of sea, two huge bodies of troops face each other: the nearer Pandya lines braced around elephants, the farther mass marked by mixed Chera and Chola standards.

dialogue.text: Talaiyalanganam. Its exact spot is lost to us, but Sangam verses fix it as a coastal field where Chera and Chola turned together to face the Pandya spear.

i18n.hi: तलैयालंगानम। इसकी ठीक जगह हम खो चुके हैं, पर संगम पद्य इसे तटीय मैदान बताते हैं, जहाँ चेरा और चोल मिलकर पांड्य के भाले के सामने खड़े हुए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nedunjeliyan in his chariot addressing his front ranks just before battle
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan stands in his chariot before the front ranks, spear raised, his war crown catching the light as grim Pandya soldiers and elephant mahouts look to him in silence.

dialogue.speaker: nedunjeliyan_ii
dialogue.text: Before this sun sets, let the bards decide whose name survives.

i18n.hi: इस सूरज के डूबने से पहले, भाट तय कर दें कि किसका नाम बचा रहेगा।

panels.shot: kinetic wide shot of battle lines surging forward, elephants and chariots charging
panels.action: Lines of armored elephants lumber forward, chariots race alongside, and foot soldiers surge in a thick cloud of dust, spears leveled toward the oncoming Chera-Chola host.

dialogue.text: The poems do not spare the fury: chariots flashing like lightning, war-drums like thunder, elephants pushing into walls of shields as dust swallowed the cries of men.

i18n.hi: कविताएँ क्रोध नहीं छुपातीं: बिजली-सी चमकती रथों की कतारें, गर्जन जैसे युद्ध-नगाड़े, ढालों की दीवारों को धकेलते हाथी, और धूल में गुम होती पुरुषों की चीखें।

panels.shot: medium action shot of Nedunjeliyan in combat on his chariot, spear extended toward unseen foes
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan leans from his racing chariot, spear thrusting toward an unseen enemy, his face fierce yet controlled as his driver strains at the reins.

dialogue.text: Maduraikanci and Purananuru agree on this much: the young Pandya did not hide in the rear. They place him in the whirl of chariots, where lines buckled around him.

i18n.hi: मदुरैकांजी और पुरनानूरु एक बात पर एकजुट हैं: युवा पांड्य पीछे नहीं छिपा। वे उसे रथों के भँवर के बीच रखते हैं, जहाँ मोर्चे उसके चारों ओर टूटते-मुड़ते दिखते हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of the opposing army’s center faltering and beginning to break
panels.action: In the midst of swirling dust, the central block of the allied army wavers; shields tilt, men glance back, and parts of the line begin to twist and break away.

dialogue.text: Against this pressure, Sangam verses say, the Chera-Chola center wavered. Once it bent, it broke, and the alliance turned to flight across the salt-scented plain.

i18n.hi: इस दबाव के सामने, संगम कविताएँ कहती हैं, चेरा–चोल की बीच की पंक्ति डगमगाई। झुकी तो टूटी, और साँठगाँठ नमक-सुगंधी मैदान पर भागती भीड़ बन गई।

panels.shot: medium shot of Nedunjeliyan overseeing the capture of a Chera king, shown being disarmed by Pandya guards
panels.action: On a trampled field at dusk, Nedunjeliyan stands tall as weary Pandya guards respectfully disarm a regal, exhausted Chera king, who is surrounded but unstruck.

dialogue.text: Here the bards grow precise. They sing that a Chera king fell into Pandya hands at Talaiyalanganam, seized alive amid the rout and taken from the field as a living trophy.

i18n.hi: यहाँ भाट एकदम साफ हो जाते हैं। वे गाते हैं कि एक चेरा राजा तलैयालंगानम में पांड्य के हाथ लगा, भगदड़ के बीच ज़िंदा पकड़ा गया, और ज़िंदा ही विजय-निशानी बनकर ले जाया गया।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Nedunjeliyan and the captured Chera king briefly locking eyes
panels.action: Nedunjeliyan and the captured Chera ruler face each other at close quarters, the Pandya king steady and unreadable, the Chera proud but resigned, their entourages tense behind them.

dialogue.text: The poems do not record exact words between captor and captive, nor the full fate of the Chera. They only linger on the moment when one crown stood subdued before another.

i18n.hi: कविताएँ बंदी और बंदी बनाने वाले के बीच के सही शब्द नहीं बतातीं, न चेरा की पूरी नियति। वे बस उस पल पर ठहर जाती हैं, जब एक मुकुट दूसरे के आगे झुका खड़ा था।

panels.shot: wide shot of triumphant return procession entering Madurai with elephants and spoils
panels.action: A grand procession enters Madurai at sunset: elephants adorned, carts piled with war-booty, and a guarded royal palanquin; crowds throng the streets as Nedunjeliyan rides at the head.

dialogue.text: When Nedunjeliyan returned to Madurai, the court poet Mankudi Maruthanar wove his name with Talaiyalanganam, praising him as the breaker of an alliance and the bringer of a royal captive.

i18n.hi: जब नेडुंजेलियन मदुरै लौटा, तो दरबारी कवि मांकुडी मरुथानार ने उसका नाम तलैयालंगानम के साथ बुन दिया, उसे साँठगाँठ तोड़ने वाला और राजबंदी लाने वाला कहकर गाया।

panels.shot: intimate interior shot of Nedunjeliyan in audience hall rewarding poets with gifts
panels.action: In the palace hall, Nedunjeliyan gently places a heavy gold neck ornament on a kneeling poet’s shoulders, while other bards stand waiting, palm-leaf manuscripts in hand.

dialogue.text: The Purananuru verses that praise his spear also describe his gifts. Bards left his hall heavy with gold and memory, carrying his war into song that outlived the clang of arms.

i18n.hi: पुरनानूरु की जो पंक्तियाँ उसके भाले की महिमा गाती हैं, वही उसके दान का रंग भी दिखाती हैं। भाट उसके सभामंडप से सोने और यादों से लदे लौटते, उसकी लड़ाइयों को गीतों में ढालते, जो हथियारों की ठनकार से ज़्यादा दिन जिंदा रहे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a later scholar in a study, palm-leaf manuscripts spread out, with a faint superimposed image of Nedunjeliyan
panels.action: Centuries later, a scholar sits by an oil lamp, palm-leaf manuscripts of Maduraikanci and other poems laid out before him, while a faint ghostlike image of Nedunjeliyan on his chariot seems to hover above the leaves.

dialogue.text: Modern historians handle these songs with care. Praise exaggerates, dates blur, numbers swell. Yet when many poets, in different voices, recall the same field and the same captive king, memory hardens toward fact.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक इतिहासकार इन गीतों को सँभालकर छूते हैं। प्रशंसा बढ़ा-चढ़ा देती है, तिथियाँ धुँधली पड़ती हैं, आँकड़े फूल जाते हैं। फिर भी जब कई कवि, अलग-अलग आवाज़ों में, एक ही मैदान और एक ही बंदी राजा को याद करते हैं, तो याद धीरे-धीरे सच की ओर सख्त हो जाती है।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the empty coastal plain at twilight, with faint overlays of three crowns fading into the sky
panels.action: The coastal plain of Talaiyalanganam lies empty at twilight, waves faintly visible in the distance; above the darkening sky, the ghosted symbols of the three crowns appear and slowly fade.

dialogue.text: Of Nedunjeliyan we see most clearly a single desperate test—a march into rival land, a broken alliance, a captive crown—and learn how, in the Sangam world, one perilous choice could define a reign for a thousand years.

i18n.hi: नेडुंजेलियन में हम सबसे साफ एक ही हताश परीक्षा देखते हैं—दुश्मन की धरती की ओर एक कूच, टूटी हुई साँठगाँठ, झुका हुआ मुकुट—और समझते हैं कि संगम दुनिया में एक जोखिम भरा फ़ैसला कैसे हज़ार साल के लिए किसी राज को परिभाषित कर सकता था।

subtitle_i18n.hi: जब तीन मुकुट नमक-हवा वाले मैदानों पर भिड़े
